title: Developing Indigenous Capabilities for Artificial Intelligence Solutions
what_it_is: Developing Indigenous Capabilities for Artificial Intelligence Solutions

sections.label: AI foundation model capabilities plan
sections.summary: Singapore has strong AI researchers working on foundation models, and it is not usually necessary to rely solely on indigenous capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether there exists a whole-of-Government plan to develop indigenous capabilities in creating and deploying artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models, including establishing a National Foundation Model Research Institute, so as to help local researchers build core AI foundation model expertise; and (b) if such an AI foundation model plan already exists, what are its core and strategic aims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We generally rank among the top 10 countries based on publications at leading AI conferences across areas, such as natural language processing and computer vision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As such, Singapore has a strong base of AI researchers who are already working on various aspects of foundation models (FMs), such as helping FMs better understand visual and audio inputs, evaluating the performance of FMs and developing FMs that are more suited for regional use cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: It is not usually necessary or beneficial to rely solely on indigenous capabilities to advance our economic interests.

sections.label: Doing both approaches
sections.summary: Large continent-sized countries do both, and FMs' potential to enhance productivity and enable new services is recognised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And, in truth, you have to do both and even large continent-sized countries are doing both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We do recognise the potential of FMs to significantly enhance productivity to enable new services.

sections.label: SEA-LION foundation models phased
sections.summary: AI Singapore is supporting SEA-LION, building a family of FMs in a phased manner, with two small ones developed so far.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But we do so in a prudent and phased manner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These efforts are relatively nascent and we will be examining our plans on how to scale up further with details to be announced later this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are supporting an initiative to build our own family of FMs through AI Singapore, named SEA-LION, or Southeast Asian languages In One Network, and training to better address regional use cases, which is a gap in existing FMs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we are building these models in a phased manner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have developed two small ones so far.

sections.label: Combination of indigenous and outsourcing
sections.summary: The issue is characterised as an appropriate combination of indigenous capabilities and outsourcing, a journey already begun.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: My key point then, Sir, is that I would characterise the issue not as either indigenous capabilities or outsourcing but, in truth, the appropriate combination of both and we have already begun on this journey.
